cite.hochreiter1997.raw: [13] Sepp Hochreiter and Jürgen Schmidhuber. Long short-term memory. Neural computation, 9(8):1735–1780, 1997.
cite.hochreiter1997.title: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)
cite.hochreiter1997.significance: Introduced a recurrent memory architecture with gates that help retain information across long sequences. It made recurrent sequence modeling more practical.
cite.hochreiter1997.connection: Establishes the recurrent-model family that the Transformer aims to replace. The link is historical motivation, rather than an LSTM component inside the Transformer.

cite.gruEval14.raw: [7] Junyoung Chung, Çaglar Gülçehre, Kyunghyun Cho, and Yoshua Bengio. Empirical evaluation of gated recurrent neural networks on sequence modeling. CoRR, abs/1412.3555, 2014.
cite.gruEval14.title: Empirical Evaluation of Gated Recurrent Neural Networks on Sequence Modeling
cite.gruEval14.significance: Compared gated recurrent units and LSTM-style networks on sequence tasks, helping evaluate alternatives for retaining information over time.
cite.gruEval14.connection: Provides background on gated recurrent networks. The Transformer replaces their sequential processing with attention-based layers.

cite.sutskever14.raw: [35] Ilya Sutskever, Oriol Vinyals, and Quoc VV Le. Sequence to sequence learning with neural networks. In Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, pages 3104–3112, 2014.
cite.sutskever14.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
cite.sutskever14.significance: Demonstrated an encoder-decoder approach that maps one sequence into another, including machine translation.
cite.sutskever14.connection: Provides the encoder-decoder problem setup. The Transformer retains the broad input-to-output structure while changing the internal computation.

cite.bahdanau2014neural.raw: [2] Dzmitry Bahdanau, Kyunghyun Cho, and Yoshua Bengio. Neural machine translation by jointly learning to align and translate. CoRR, abs/1409.0473, 2014.
cite.bahdanau2014neural.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
cite.bahdanau2014neural.significance: Let a translation decoder attend to relevant source positions instead of relying only on one fixed sentence representation. This is a central precursor of neural attention.
cite.bahdanau2014neural.connection: Provides an attention-based translation precursor. The Transformer extends attention into its main architecture and removes recurrent layers; some occurrences also compare attention scoring functions.

cite.cho2014learning.raw: [5] Kyunghyun Cho, Bart van Merrienboer, Caglar Gulcehre, Fethi Bougares, Holger Schwenk, and Yoshua Bengio. Learning phrase representations using rnn encoder-decoder for statistical machine translation. CoRR, abs/1406.1078, 2014.
cite.cho2014learning.title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation
cite.cho2014learning.significance: Developed recurrent encoder-decoder representations for translating phrases.
cite.cho2014learning.connection: Supports the encoder-decoder lineage. The Transformer preserves the overall translation setup, with attention replacing the recurrent machinery.

cite.wu2016google.raw: [38] Yonghui Wu, Mike Schuster, Zhifeng Chen, Quoc V Le, Mohammad Norouzi, Wolfgang Macherey, Maxim Krikun, Yuan Cao, Qin Gao, Klaus Macherey, et al. Google’s neural machine translation system: Bridging the gap between human and machine translation. arXiv preprint arXiv:1609.08144, 2016.
cite.wu2016google.title: Google’s Neural Machine Translation System
cite.wu2016google.significance: Described a large neural translation system with practical modeling, training and decoding choices.
cite.wu2016google.connection: Serves as prior translation work and a comparison system. In decoding discussions, it is also the source of a length-penalty approach.

cite.luong2015effective.raw: [24] Minh-Thang Luong, Hieu Pham, and Christopher D Manning. Effective approaches to attentionbased neural machine translation. arXiv preprint arXiv:1508.04025, 2015.
cite.luong2015effective.title: Effective Approaches to Attention-based Neural Machine Translation
cite.luong2015effective.significance: Studied practical global and local attention approaches for recurrent translation models.
cite.luong2015effective.connection: Supplies attention-based translation background and comparison points. The Transformer uses attention throughout rather than attaching it to a recurrent model.

cite.jozefowicz2016exploring.raw: [15] Rafal Jozefowicz, Oriol Vinyals, Mike Schuster, Noam Shazeer, and Yonghui Wu. Exploring the limits of language modeling. arXiv preprint arXiv:1602.02410, 2016.
cite.jozefowicz2016exploring.title: Exploring the Limits of Language Modeling
cite.jozefowicz2016exploring.significance: Investigated the performance and practical design of large recurrent language models.
cite.jozefowicz2016exploring.connection: Shows the strength of earlier recurrent modeling, helping motivate a more parallel architecture.

cite.Kuchaiev2017Factorization.raw: [21] Oleksii Kuchaiev and Boris Ginsburg. Factorization tricks for LSTM networks. arXiv preprint arXiv:1703.10722, 2017.
cite.Kuchaiev2017Factorization.title: Factorization Tricks for LSTM Networks
cite.Kuchaiev2017Factorization.significance: Explored compact factorizations to make LSTM computation more efficient.
cite.Kuchaiev2017Factorization.connection: Illustrates attempts to speed up recurrent models. The Transformer argues that these still leave the fundamental sequential dependency in place.

cite.shazeer2017outrageously.raw: [32] Noam Shazeer, Azalia Mirhoseini, Krzysztof Maziarz, Andy Davis, Quoc Le, Geoffrey Hinton, and Jeff Dean. Outrageously large neural networks: The sparsely-gated mixture-of-experts layer. arXiv preprint arXiv:1701.06538, 2017.
cite.shazeer2017outrageously.title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer
cite.shazeer2017outrageously.significance: Routes inputs to selected expert subnetworks, increasing model capacity without activating all parameters for every input.
cite.shazeer2017outrageously.connection: Shows conditional computation as another efficiency strategy. This is motivation in the introduction, not a claim that the original Transformer uses a mixture-of-experts layer.

cite.structuredAttentionNetworks.raw: [19] Yoon Kim, Carl Denton, Luong Hoang, and Alexander M. Rush. Structured attention networks. In International Conference on Learning Representations, 2017.
cite.structuredAttentionNetworks.title: Structured Attention Networks
cite.structuredAttentionNetworks.significance: Explored differentiable attention mechanisms that can represent structured relationships.
cite.structuredAttentionNetworks.connection: Supports the broader attention research background. Its role here is prior art rather than the exact attention layer used by the Transformer.

cite.decomposableAttnModel.raw: [27] Ankur Parikh, Oscar Täckström, Dipanjan Das, and Jakob Uszkoreit. A decomposable attention model. In Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, 2016.
cite.decomposableAttnModel.title: A Decomposable Attention Model
cite.decomposableAttnModel.significance: Used attention-based comparisons for natural-language inference with a simple decomposable architecture.
cite.decomposableAttnModel.connection: Provides a prior example of attention operating without a recurrent network, qualifying the historical background of the Transformer’s design.

cite.extendedngpu.raw: [16] Łukasz Kaiser and Samy Bengio. Can active memory replace attention? In Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, (NIPS), 2016.
cite.extendedngpu.title: Can Active Memory Replace Attention?
cite.extendedngpu.significance: Explored memory-based neural sequence computation as an alternative design direction.
cite.extendedngpu.connection: Provides an earlier attempt to reduce sequential computation. It helps position the Transformer among alternative sequence architectures.

cite.NalBytenet2017.raw: [18] Nal Kalchbrenner, Lasse Espeholt, Karen Simonyan, Aaron van den Oord, Alex Graves, and Koray Kavukcuoglu. Neural machine translation in linear time. arXiv preprint arXiv:1610.10099v2, 2017.
cite.NalBytenet2017.title: Neural Machine Translation in Linear Time (ByteNet)
cite.NalBytenet2017.significance: Used convolutional sequence modeling to support more parallel translation computation.
cite.NalBytenet2017.connection: Acts as a competing architectural approach. The Transformer contrasts convolutional dependency paths with the shorter paths available through self-attention.

cite.JonasFaceNet2017.raw: [9] Jonas Gehring, Michael Auli, David Grangier, Denis Yarats, and Yann N. Dauphin. Convolutional sequence to sequence learning. arXiv preprint arXiv:1705.03122v2, 2017.
cite.JonasFaceNet2017.title: Convolutional Sequence to Sequence Learning
cite.JonasFaceNet2017.significance: Built a convolutional encoder-decoder for sequence generation and translation.
cite.JonasFaceNet2017.connection: Provides a parallel sequence-modeling comparison. It is also relevant to the comparison between learned and sinusoidal position information.

cite.hochreiter2001gradient.raw: [12] Sepp Hochreiter, Yoshua Bengio, Paolo Frasconi, and Jürgen Schmidhuber. Gradient flow in recurrent nets: the difficulty of learning long-term dependencies, 2001.
cite.hochreiter2001gradient.title: Gradient Flow in Recurrent Nets: The Difficulty of Learning Long-Term Dependencies
cite.hochreiter2001gradient.significance: Examined why training recurrent networks to capture long-range relationships is difficult.
cite.hochreiter2001gradient.connection: Motivates shorter paths between distant sequence positions. This supports the architectural argument for attention, not a new training algorithm in this paper.

cite.cheng2016long.raw: [4] Jianpeng Cheng, Li Dong, and Mirella Lapata. Long short-term memory-networks for machine reading. arXiv preprint arXiv:1601.06733, 2016.
cite.cheng2016long.title: Long Short-Term Memory-Networks for Machine Reading
cite.cheng2016long.significance: Explored memory and attention mechanisms for representing text in machine reading.
cite.cheng2016long.connection: Supports the claim that within-sequence attention had already been useful. The Transformer builds on this research direction at the architecture level.

cite.paulus2017deep.raw: [28] Romain Paulus, Caiming Xiong, and Richard Socher. A deep reinforced model for abstractive summarization. arXiv preprint arXiv:1705.04304, 2017.
cite.paulus2017deep.title: A Deep Reinforced Model for Abstractive Summarization
cite.paulus2017deep.significance: Combined neural summarization with reinforcement-learning-based training and attention-related mechanisms.
cite.paulus2017deep.connection: Provides a prior application of attention to summarization. It is background evidence, rather than the Transformer’s training objective.

cite.lin2017structured.raw: [22] Zhouhan Lin, Minwei Feng, Cicero Nogueira dos Santos, Mo Yu, Bing Xiang, Bowen Zhou, and Yoshua Bengio. A structured self-attentive sentence embedding. arXiv preprint arXiv:1703.03130, 2017.
cite.lin2017structured.title: A Structured Self-Attentive Sentence Embedding
cite.lin2017structured.significance: Used self-attention to produce sentence representations with several aspects of the sentence emphasized.
cite.lin2017structured.connection: Supplies a self-attention precedent for sentence representations. The Transformer uses related ideas across its encoder and decoder layers.

cite.sukhbaatar2015.raw: [34] Sainbayar Sukhbaatar, Arthur Szlam, Jason Weston, and Rob Fergus. End-to-end memory networks. In C. Cortes, N. D. Lawrence, D. D. Lee, M. Sugiyama, and R. Garnett, editors, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 28, pages 2440–2448. Curran Associates, Inc., 2015.
cite.sukhbaatar2015.title: End-to-End Memory Networks
cite.sukhbaatar2015.significance: Made attention-based memory access trainable end to end, including for question-answering tasks.
cite.sukhbaatar2015.connection: Provides a prior attention-and-memory approach and helps frame what is distinctive about the Transformer’s sequence architecture.

cite.neural_gpu.raw: [17] Łukasz Kaiser and Ilya Sutskever. Neural GPUs learn algorithms. In International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR), 2016.
cite.neural_gpu.title: Neural GPUs Learn Algorithms
cite.neural_gpu.significance: Studied a parallel neural architecture for learning algorithmic sequence tasks.
cite.neural_gpu.connection: Offers another architecture to compare with the Transformer’s goal of reducing sequential computation.

cite.graves2013generating.raw: [10] Alex Graves. Generating sequences with recurrent neural networks. arXiv preprint arXiv:1308.0850, 2013.
cite.graves2013generating.title: Generating Sequences with Recurrent Neural Networks
cite.graves2013generating.significance: Studied recurrent models that generate sequences one step at a time.
cite.graves2013generating.connection: Supports the autoregressive generation setup: future output tokens depend on earlier output tokens, even though Transformer training can be parallelized.

cite.he2016deep.raw: [11] Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren, and Jian Sun. Deep residual learning for image recognition. In Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, pages 770–778, 2016.
cite.he2016deep.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
cite.he2016deep.significance: Introduced residual connections that let layers learn changes relative to their inputs, helping train much deeper networks.
cite.he2016deep.connection: The Transformer uses residual connections around sublayers. This is a borrowed architectural ingredient, distinct from its attention contribution.

cite.layernorm2016.raw: [1] Jimmy Lei Ba, Jamie Ryan Kiros, and Geoffrey E Hinton. Layer normalization. arXiv preprint arXiv:1607.06450, 2016.
cite.layernorm2016.title: Layer Normalization
cite.layernorm2016.significance: Normalizes activations within a layer for each example, helping stabilize neural-network training.
cite.layernorm2016.connection: The Transformer uses layer normalization with its residual sublayers. It is a training-stability ingredient in the architecture.

cite.DBLP:journals/corr/BritzGLL17.raw: [3] Denny Britz, Anna Goldie, Minh-Thang Luong, and Quoc V. Le. Massive exploration of neural machine translation architectures. CoRR, abs/1703.03906, 2017.
cite.DBLP:journals/corr/BritzGLL17.title: Massive Exploration of Neural Machine Translation Architectures
cite.DBLP:journals/corr/BritzGLL17.significance: Systematically compared design choices for neural translation architectures.
cite.DBLP:journals/corr/BritzGLL17.connection: Provides empirical context for choices in attention-based translation, including the comparison of attention scoring mechanisms.

cite.press2016using.raw: [30] Ofir Press and Lior Wolf. Using the output embedding to improve language models. arXiv preprint arXiv:1608.05859, 2016.
cite.press2016using.title: Using the Output Embedding to Improve Language Models
cite.press2016using.significance: Studied sharing input and output embedding weights in language models.
cite.press2016using.connection: The Transformer shares embedding and output-projection weights. This citation credits that parameter-sharing technique.

cite.sennrich2015neural.raw: [31] Rico Sennrich, Barry Haddow, and Alexandra Birch. Neural machine translation of rare words with subword units. arXiv preprint arXiv:1508.07909, 2015.
cite.sennrich2015neural.title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units
cite.sennrich2015neural.significance: Used subword segmentation to represent rare words through smaller reusable pieces.
cite.sennrich2015neural.connection: Supplies the subword tokenization approach used to prepare translation data. This concerns input representation, rather than attention computation.

cite.xception2016.raw: [6] Francois Chollet. Xception: Deep learning with depthwise separable convolutions. arXiv preprint arXiv:1610.02357, 2016.
cite.xception2016.title: Xception: Deep Learning with Depthwise Separable Convolutions
cite.xception2016.significance: Developed an image-network architecture based on depthwise separable convolutions.
cite.xception2016.connection: Provides a convolutional efficiency comparison in the architecture discussion. It is not a claim that the Transformer uses the Xception image model.

cite.kingma2014adam.raw: [20] Diederik Kingma and Jimmy Ba. Adam: A method for stochastic optimization. In ICLR, 2015.
cite.kingma2014adam.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
cite.kingma2014adam.significance: Adapts parameter updates using running estimates of gradient statistics. It became a widely used neural-network optimizer.
cite.kingma2014adam.connection: The Transformer is trained with Adam. This is the optimization method used to fit its parameters, separate from the attention architecture.

cite.DBLP:journals/corr/ZhouCWLX16.raw: [39] Jie Zhou, Ying Cao, Xuguang Wang, Peng Li, and Wei Xu. Deep recurrent models with fast-forward connections for neural machine translation. CoRR, abs/1606.04199, 2016.
cite.DBLP:journals/corr/ZhouCWLX16.title: Deep Recurrent Models with Fast-Forward Connections for Neural Machine Translation
cite.DBLP:journals/corr/ZhouCWLX16.significance: Studied deep recurrent translation models with additional connections to support training.
cite.DBLP:journals/corr/ZhouCWLX16.connection: Provides a recurrent translation comparison system in the reported translation results.

cite.srivastava2014dropout.raw: [33] Nitish Srivastava, Geoffrey E Hinton, Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and Ruslan Salakhutdinov. Dropout: a simple way to prevent neural networks from overfitting. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 15(1):1929–1958, 2014.
cite.srivastava2014dropout.title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
cite.srivastava2014dropout.significance: Randomly drops units during training to discourage overly dependent features and improve generalization.
cite.srivastava2014dropout.connection: The Transformer uses dropout as regularization. It helps control overfitting during training.

cite.DBLP:journals/corr/SzegedyVISW15.raw: [36] Christian Szegedy, Vincent Vanhoucke, Sergey Ioffe, Jonathon Shlens, and Zbigniew Wojna. Rethinking the inception architecture for computer vision. CoRR, abs/1512.00567, 2015.
cite.DBLP:journals/corr/SzegedyVISW15.title: Rethinking the Inception Architecture for Computer Vision
cite.DBLP:journals/corr/SzegedyVISW15.significance: Explored improvements to an image-classification architecture, including label smoothing as a regularization technique.
cite.DBLP:journals/corr/SzegedyVISW15.connection: The Transformer credits this work for label smoothing, which softens training targets. The borrowed ingredient is not the Inception image architecture.

cite.KVparse15.raw: [37] Vinyals & Kaiser, Koo, Petrov, Sutskever, and Hinton. Grammar as a foreign language. In Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 2015.
cite.KVparse15.title: Grammar as a Foreign Language
cite.KVparse15.significance: Treated syntactic parsing as a sequence-to-sequence task.
cite.KVparse15.connection: Provides a prior sequence-modeling baseline and related parsing training setup. It helps test whether the Transformer generalizes beyond translation.

cite.marcus1993building.raw: [25] Mitchell P Marcus, Mary Ann Marcinkiewicz, and Beatrice Santorini. Building a large annotated corpus of english: The penn treebank. Computational linguistics, 19(2):313–330, 1993.
cite.marcus1993building.title: Building a Large Annotated Corpus of English: The Penn Treebank
cite.marcus1993building.significance: Created an important annotated English corpus used to train and evaluate language-analysis systems.
cite.marcus1993building.connection: Supplies the parsing dataset. It contributes evaluation material, not a competing neural architecture.

cite.petrov-EtAl:2006:ACL.raw: [29] Slav Petrov, Leon Barrett, Romain Thibaux, and Dan Klein. Learning accurate, compact, and interpretable tree annotation. In Proceedings of the 21st International Conference on Computational Linguistics and 44th Annual Meeting of the ACL, pages 433–440. ACL, July 2006.
cite.petrov-EtAl:2006:ACL.title: Learning Accurate, Compact, and Interpretable Tree Annotation
cite.petrov-EtAl:2006:ACL.significance: Studied automatically refined tree annotations for statistical parsing.
cite.petrov-EtAl:2006:ACL.connection: Provides a parsing comparison system, helping assess the Transformer on a structured prediction task.

cite.zhu-EtAl:2013:ACL.raw: [40] Muhua Zhu, Yue Zhang, Wenliang Chen, Min Zhang, and Jingbo Zhu. Fast and accurate shift-reduce constituent parsing. In Proceedings of the 51st Annual Meeting of the ACL (Volume 1: Long Papers), pages 434–443. ACL, August 2013.
cite.zhu-EtAl:2013:ACL.title: Fast and Accurate Shift-Reduce Constituent Parsing
cite.zhu-EtAl:2013:ACL.significance: Developed an efficient constituent-parsing approach based on shift-reduce decisions.
cite.zhu-EtAl:2013:ACL.connection: Provides parsing baseline results. Its contribution here is a comparison point for the Transformer’s parsing experiment.

cite.dyer-rnng:16.raw: [8] Chris Dyer, Adhiguna Kuncoro, Miguel Ballesteros, and Noah A. Smith. Recurrent neural network grammars. In Proc. of NAACL, 2016.
cite.dyer-rnng:16.title: Recurrent Neural Network Grammars
cite.dyer-rnng:16.significance: Combined recurrent neural modeling with explicit grammatical structure for parsing and language modeling.
cite.dyer-rnng:16.connection: Provides a strong structured parsing comparison. It helps show both the Transformer’s performance and the limits of the reported comparison.

cite.huang-harper:2009:EMNLP.raw: [14] Zhongqiang Huang and Mary Harper. Self-training PCFG grammars with latent annotations across languages. In Proceedings of the 2009 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, pages 832–841. ACL, August 2009.
cite.huang-harper:2009:EMNLP.title: Self-Training PCFG Grammars with Latent Annotations Across Languages
cite.huang-harper:2009:EMNLP.significance: Studied self-training for parsers with latent grammatical annotations.
cite.huang-harper:2009:EMNLP.connection: Provides a semi-supervised parsing baseline, rather than a component of the Transformer.

cite.mcclosky-etAl:2006:NAACL.raw: [26] David McClosky, Eugene Charniak, and Mark Johnson. Effective self-training for parsing. In Proceedings of the Human Language Technology Conference of the NAACL, Main Conference, pages 152–159. ACL, June 2006.
cite.mcclosky-etAl:2006:NAACL.title: Effective Self-Training for Parsing
cite.mcclosky-etAl:2006:NAACL.significance: Used parser-generated analyses of additional data to improve parsing through self-training.
cite.mcclosky-etAl:2006:NAACL.connection: Provides a semi-supervised parsing comparison. The citation situates the Transformer’s parsing results among earlier uses of extra training data.

cite.multiseq2seq.raw: [23] Minh-Thang Luong, Quoc V. Le, Ilya Sutskever, Oriol Vinyals, and Lukasz Kaiser. Multi-task sequence to sequence learning. arXiv preprint arXiv:1511.06114, 2015.
cite.multiseq2seq.title: Multi-task Sequence to Sequence Learning
cite.multiseq2seq.significance: Studied sharing sequence-to-sequence learning across tasks.
cite.multiseq2seq.connection: Provides a multi-task parsing comparison in the evaluation table; it is not the Transformer’s own training recipe.

occurrences.excerpt: The two most commonly used attention functions are additive attention [2], and dot-product (multiplicative) attention. Dot-product attention is identical to our algorithm, except for the scaling factor of 1 √dk . Additive attention computes the compatibility function using a feed-forward network with a single hidden layer. While the two are similar in theoretical complexity, dot-product attention is much faster and more space-efficient in practice, since it can be implemented using highly optimized matrix multiplication code.
occurrences.rationale: Here the authors compare additive attention with dot-product attention. Bahdanau’s work supplies the additive-attention precedent; the Transformer chooses scaled dot-product attention.

occurrences.excerpt: While for small values of dk the two mechanisms perform similarly, additive attention outperforms dot product attention without scaling for larger values of dk [3].
